items.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019
items.q: the great choreographer Agnes DeMille said when there’s a pattern there’s an expectation.

ctx.x: When you’re improvising. Good one. That was quick. If you’re improvising and you do a particular thing and it worked, then you’re moving on. You know there’s this term like we’re in the moment. But there was a moment a few seconds ago or a few measures ago then you did something, can I safely say that that doesn’t leave your memory? Because you may want to do it again or you may not want to do it again.

Well I aspire toward being in a place where I can actually make that decision, rather than have me just speak on in the other place. When you have the larger picture you realize that it’s happened, then as you said, you see whether it’s relevant. If it has relevance as you move forward or not. But yes, if it’s not too far away I might remember it and use it or not. So I don’t know quite how to get to that or change it. We all, we have patterns you know. We all are — we perceive patterns, amazingly, through a…
just being conscious of those expectations and then translating it to my little thing or our little thing about playing jazz you know. As I said it can be any aspect of art or life you know.
